Superclass omics

Source: R/omics-class.R
omics.Rd

OmicFlow is constructed around the main superclass omics that in turn is inherited by metagenomics and proteomics, that offer additional fields or methods. The superclass omics contains both public and private methods, only the public componenents are documented, whereas the private methods can be accessed via omics$private_methods, which is not supported.

The omics class components use Matrix and data.table in the background for fast loading and data wrangling, these data structures return the data by reference, so does the R6 class, therefore classes in OmicFlow do not create copies of the object unless called via $copy().

All classes needs to be first initialised via the $new() method and require the metaData and countData field components. Alternatively, you can also initialise with only the metaData and later add the other fields via the active binding, but this will not create a back-up and is not advised! For more hands-on examples see Getting Started with OmicFlow.

Input requirements

Every class in OmicFlow requires at least a metaData and countData field to be specified. The metaData must contain a SAMPLE_ID and optionally a SAMPLEPAIR_ID, see section "Metadata validation" below.

The countData can be both a matrix or data frame. If the original contains rownames, then these will become the FEATURE_ID in featureData (automatically created), otherwise a random feature identifier is assigned. If the countData is a filetype or a data frame with both matching sample identifiers in SAMPLE_ID and other additional columns, then these will be automatically split, columns matching the SAMPLE_ID will be placed in the countData, any other columns will be placed in front of the FEATURE_ID column in featureData.

Metadata validation

Every class in OmicFlow begins by validating the sample metadata. This validation checks that sample identifiers match the sample IDs present in the abundance tables.

The validation rules are defined in JSON format in the omics class. Metadata can be supplied as either:

  • A CSV or TSV file.

  • A data.table.

In both cases, metadata must include a header row and follow a one-row-per-sample structure. For file inputs, the header must be on the first line. Columns not described below are permitted and are ignored during metadata validation.

Minimum requirement

The metadata must contain a SAMPLE_ID column.

  • Each row must have a unique, non-empty sample identifier.

  • Sample identifiers cannot contain spaces; use underscores (_) or dashes (-) instead.

Example metadata:


SAMPLE_ID  SAMPLEPAIR_ID  CONTRAST_Treatment  VARIABLE_Age
S1         P1             Drug                42
S2         P1             Placebo             36
S3         P2             Drug                51

Column types and naming rules

Required column

ColumnTypeRules
SAMPLE_IDstringUnique, non-empty, no spaces; one identifier per sample row

Optional standard columns

ColumnTypeRules
SAMPLEPAIR_IDstringOptional; no spaces. Used for samples that are paired or originate from the same individual or subject.

Some functions require a SAMEPLEPAIR_ID in the metaData when paired = TRUE is used. The user can add or remove the SAMPLEPAIR_ID at anytime to the metaData via active binding.

Pattern-based columns

Additional variables can be defined with special column-name prefixes:

  • CONTRAST_...: Grouping or category labels for differential comparisons. For example, CONTRAST_Treatment may contain Drug and Placebo.

  • VARIABLE_...: Numeric or string variables for statistical analysis. For example, VARIABLE_Age may contain values such as 42 and 51.

Pattern-based columns are only used in $autoFlow(). Currently, only columns with the CONTRAST_ prefix are supported.

Active bindings

metaData

A data.table with SAMPLE_ID column.

featureData

A data.table with FEATURE_ID column.

countData

A sparseMatrix with rownames matching FEATURE_ID of featureData and colnames matching SAMPLE_ID of countData.

omics$new()

Usage

omics$new(metaData = NULL, countData = NULL, featureData = NULL)

Arguments

metaData

A path to an existing file, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

countData

A path to an existing file, Matrix, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

featureData

A path to an existing file, data.table or data.frame (default: NULL).

Returns

A new omics object.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

## Method 1: load from filepath
metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file
)

## Method 2: Load from data.frame or matrix
n_cols <- 5
n_rows <- 100
n_vals <- n_cols * n_rows
metadata <- data.frame("SAMPLE_ID" = paste0("Sample_", 1:n_cols))
features <- data.frame("FEATURE_ID" = paste0("protein_", 1:n_rows))
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
 1:n_vals, nrow = n_rows, ncol = n_cols,
 dimnames = list(features$FEATURE_ID, metadata$SAMPLE_ID)
)

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 featureData = features, # optional
 countData = counts
)

## Method 3: you have features and counts in a single data.frame
metadata <- data.frame(SAMPLE_ID = c("S1", "S2", "S3"))
counts <- data.frame(
 S1 = c(2,3,0),
 S2 = c(2,"",1),
 S3 = c(2,1,NA),
 proteins = c("ZEB1", "ZEB2", "MAPK")
)

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 countData = counts
)

omics$copy()

This method is very similar to the existing $clone() function, except it also creates a new save of the back-up of each class that is created when $new() is called and can be reverted to via $reset()

Usage

omics$copy(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

A boolean value to create a shallow or deep copy (default: FALSE).

Returns

A copy of omics object.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file
)

# Perform a modification and copy
obj$scale()

cloned <- obj$copy(deep=TRUE)
cloned$scale(method = "clr")
cloned$reset() # resets to data after clone creation.

Displays field parameters of the class via stdout.

Usage

omics$print()

Returns

A cli formatted message

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- omics$new(

)

# method 1 to call print function
obj

# method 2 to call print function
obj$print()

omics$reset()

Upon creation of a new class object (i.e. omics, metagenomics or proteomics) a backup of the original data is created. Since modification of the object is done by reference and duplicates are not made, it is possible to revert back to the unmodified data via $reset(). The methods from the super class omics also contains a private method to prevent any changes to the original object when using methods, such as ordination, alpha_diversity or foldchange.

Usage

omics$reset()

Returns

The object is modified in place and returned (invisibly). If a copy is required, please use $copy() beforehand with obj2 <- obj$copy().

Examples

library(ggplot2)
library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

taxa <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file
)

# Performs modifications
taxa$scale(transform = log2)

# resets
taxa$reset()

# An inbuilt reset function prevents unwanted modification to the taxa object.
taxa$rankstat(feature_ranks = c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Family", "Genus", "Species"))

A logical expression evaluated in the context of featureData. Rows for which the expression evaluates to TRUE are retained.

omics$samplepair_subset()

Subset samplepairs by choosing the number of unique pairs in metaData, then synchronize the object.

Usage

omics$samplepair_subset(num_unique_pairs = NULL)

Arguments

num_unique_pairs

An integer value to define the number of pairs to subset. The default is NULL, meaning the maximum number of unique pairs will be used to subset the data. Let's say you have three samples for each pair, then the num_unique_pairs will be set to 3.

Returns

The object is modified in place and returned (invisibly). If a copy is required, please use $copy() beforehand with obj2 <- obj$copy().

library("OmicFlow")

counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj$feature_merge(feature_rank = c("Kingdom", "Phylum"))

omics$scale()

Feature scaling on the countData. The $scale function is able to apply transformations element-wise on the positive values, (optional: add pseudocounts) and perform normalisation or standardisation methods.

Usage

omics$scale(
  method = "tss",
  transform = NULL,
  base = exp(1),
  pseudocount = NULL
)

Arguments

method

A character to choose a standardisation/normalisation method, options: "tss", "clr", "binary", "hellinger", "none" (default: "tss").

"tss"

Total-sum scaling. Each column is divided by their column sum, converting absolute abundance to relative abundances in range from 0 to 1.

"clr"

Centered log-ratio-like transformation. Non-zero entries are log-transformed using log and base, then each feature row is centered by subtracting by their respective geometric mean. Input counts must be strictly positive for his transformation. If pseudocount is used, then output is equal to vegan::decostand(method = "clr"), otherwise the current "clr" approximates the vegan::decostand(method = "rclr"), the main difference is that vegan replaces all zero's by NAs and then excludes them when the arithmetic mean is taken, whereas zero's in "clr" are only not used for log-transformation but preserved when taking the arithmetic mean of each feature row.

"binary"

Presence-absence transformation. Every stored non-zero count is replaced by one, while implicit zeros in the sparse matrix remain zero.

"hellinger"

Hellinger transformation. Counts are first total-sum scaled with "tss" to relative abundances, after which the square root of each non-zero value is taken.

"none"

No transformation. Typically applied when transform is used.

transform

A function to apply on the positive values of countData, skip standardisation/normalisation with method = "none" (default: NULL).

base

Input for log to use natural logarithmic scale, log2, log10 or other (default: exp(1)) in CLR.

pseudocount

A numeric value to replace zero's (default: NULL).

Returns

The object is modified in place and returned (invisibly). If a copy is required, please use $copy() beforehand with obj2 <- obj$copy().

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- metagenomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file,
)
# standard relative abundance computation
obj$scale()

# CLR
obj$reset()
obj$scale(method = "clr")

# transform
obj$reset()
obj$scale(method = "none", transform = log2)

omics$alpha_diversity()

Alpha diversity computation, statistical testing and visualisation.

It computes the alpha diversity via diversity, performs a pairwise wilcoxon statistical test given groups via the boxjitter_test.

Usage

omics$alpha_diversity(
  col_name = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  groups,
  metric = "shannon",
  Brewer.palID = "Set2",
  group_by = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  split_by = NULL,
  evenness = FALSE,
  paired = FALSE,
  p.adjust.method = "fdr"
)

Arguments

col_name

This argument has been renamed to groups for more clarity.

groups

A column name in metaData to define the contrast of interest for statistical testing and visualisation.

metric

An alpha diversity metric as input to diversity, options: "shannon", "simpson", "invsimpson" (default: "shannon").

Brewer.palID

A character name for the palette set to be applied, see brewer.pal or colormap (default: "Set2").

group_by

This argument has been renamed to split_by for more clarity

split_by

A column name to split the groups into chunks for grouped statistical test in boxjitter_test (default: NULL).

evenness

A boolean wether to divide diversity by number of species, see specnumber (default: FALSE).

paired

A boolean value to perform paired analysis in wilcox.test and samplepair subsetting via $samplepair_subset()

p.adjust.method

A character variable to specify the p.adjust.method to be used (default: "fdr").

Returns

A list of components:

data

A data.frame from diversity.

stats

A pairwise statistics from pairwise_wilcox_test.

plot

A ggplot object.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- metagenomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file,
)

plt <- obj$alpha_diversity(groups = "treatment",
                           metric = "shannon")

omics$composition()

Creates a long data.table of SAMPLE_IDs, the top 10-15 most abundant bacteria based on the feature_rank with any additional columns specified via add_cols. The $composition() method works with aggregated values by running first $feature_merge(), then sorting for the most abundant bacteria based on the row sums. The output of $composition() can be used as input to composition_plot.

Usage

omics$composition(
  feature_rank,
  feature_filter = NULL,
  col_name = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  add_cols = NULL,
  feature_top = 10,
  Brewer.palID = "RdYlBu"
)

Arguments

feature_rank

A column name in featureData to aggregate via $feature_merge().

feature_filter

A character or vector of characters to removes features by regex substring pattern matching via $feature_merge() (default: NULL).

col_name

This argument has been renamed to add_cols for more clarity.

add_cols

Optional, a column name or vector of multiple column names from metaData to add to the data list name (default": NULL).

feature_top

A wholenumber of the top features to visualize, the max is 15, due to a limit of palettes (default: 10).

Brewer.palID

A character name for the palette set to be applied, see brewer.pal or colormap (default: "RdYlBu").

Returns

A list of components:

data

A data.table of feature compositions.

palette

A setNames palette from colormap matching the top features.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- metagenomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file,
)

result <- obj$composition(feature_rank = "Genus",
                          feature_filter = c("uncultured"),
                          feature_top = 10)

plt <- composition_plot(data = result$data,
                        palette = result$palette,
                        feature_rank = "Genus")

omics$distance()

Compute a distance metric from countData

Usage

omics$distance(
  metric,
  weighted = TRUE,
  threads = 1,
  normalize = TRUE,
  base = exp(1)
)

Arguments

metric

A dissimilarity metric to be applied on the countData, options:

"bray"

bray

"jaccard"

jaccard

"cosine"

cosine

"manhattan"

manhattan

"euclidean"

euclidean

"jsd"

jsd

"canberra"

canberra

"unifrac"

unifrac

"aitchison"

The "aitchison" metric uses the $scale(method = "clr") without any pseudocounts, see $scale(), followed by euclidean dissimilarity computation.

Ref: Aitchison, J. (1986) The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and Hall, London, 416 p.

weighted

A boolean value, to use abundances (weighted = TRUE) or absence/presence (weighted=FALSE) (default: TRUE).

threads

A wholenumber, indicating the number of threads to use (default: 1).

normalize

A boolean value, whether to normalize weighted UniFrac distances to be between 0 and 1. Unweighted UniFrac is always normalized (default: TRUE).

base

Input for log to use natural logarithmic scale, log2, log10 or other (default: exp(1)).

Returns

A column x column dist object.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- metagenomics$new(
    metaData = metadata_file,
    countData = counts_file,
    featureData = features_file
)

obj$feature_subset(Kingdom == "Bacteria")
dist <- obj$distance(metric = "bray")

omics$ordination()

The $ordination() method either computes a distance matrix by specification of the metric or takes a custom distance matrix via distmat. It then computes either the pairwise PERMANOVA test on the defined contrast via group_by via pairwise_adonis or the pairwise ANOSIM test via pairwise_anosim.

Which pairwise test to compute is decided via the method argument, where "pcoa" results in the pairwise_adonis and "nmds" to pairwise_anosim.

It also visualises these results as a scree-plot (only when "pcoa" is used), scores-plot (see ordination_plot) and an anova-plot (see plot_pairwise_stats). These plots, alongisde the distance matrix, principal components are returned as a list.

Usage

omics$ordination(
  metric = "bray",
  method = "pcoa",
  group_by,
  distmat = NULL,
  weighted = TRUE,
  normalize = TRUE,
  threads = 1,
  perm_design = NULL,
  perm = 999
)

Arguments

metric

A dissimilarity or similarity metric to be applied on the countData, see $distance() (default: "bray").

method

Ordination method, options: "pcoa" or "nmds", see wcmdscale (default: "pcoa").

"pcoa"

When "pcoa" (Principal Coordinate Analysis) is chosen, a pairwise PERMANOVA test via pairwise_adonis is conducted on the contrast specified by group_by with n number of permutations, perm.

"nmds"

When "nmds" (Non-Metric Multidimensional Scaling) is chosen, a pairwise ANOSIM test via pairwise_anosim is conducted on the contrast specified by group_by with n number of permutations, perm. This method returns 2 dimensions by default, and a stress score in the pcs list name, that acts as the confidence, see metaMDS. Since only two dimensions are returned, there is no scree_plot output.

group_by

A character variable in metaData to be used for the pairwise_adonis or pairwise_anosim statistical test.

distmat

A custom distance matrix as either dist or Matrix (default: NULL).

weighted

A boolean value, whether to compute weighted or unweighted dissimilarities, see $distance() (default: TRUE).

normalize

A boolean value, wether to normalize weighted UniFrac distances to be between 0 and 1, see unifrac (default: TRUE).

threads

A wholenumber, indicating the number of threads to use (default: 1).

perm_design

A function that takes metaData and constructs a permutation design with how, see example (default: NULL).

perm

A whole number to define the number of permutations in adonis2 and anosim (default: 999).

Returns

A list of components:

distmat

A distance dissimilarity in matrix format.

stats

A statistical test as a data.frame.

pcs

principal components as a data.frame.

scree_plot

A ggplot object.

anova_plot

A ggplot object.

scores_plot

A ggplot object.

Examples

library("ggplot2")
library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- metagenomics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file,
)

pcoa_plots <- obj$ordination(metric = "bray",
                             method = "pcoa",
                             group_by = "treatment",
                             weighted = TRUE)
pcoa_plots

omics$foldchange()

Differential feature expression for both paired and non-paired data.

The function performs feature agglomeration via $feature_merge() (which can be disabled via feature_merge=FALSE), subsetting to remove NAs in condition.group via $removeNAs() and finding samplepairs when paired = TRUE is supplied via $subset_samplepairs().

The fold-changes can be computed differently based on the method and aggregate_method options. Transformations of the data should be done beforehand via $scale(). Finally, homogeneity of variance is computed based on the selected aggregate_method option. If aggregate_method = "mean" then the row_levene is applied, and if aggregate_method = "median" is used then the row_brownforsythe is applied. Any filtering of the results is left to the end-user, volcano plots are automatically added to the list name volcano_plot via volcano_plot.

Usage

omics$foldchange(
  condition.group,
  condition_A,
  condition_B,
  method = "identity",
  aggregate_method = "median",
  group_by = lifecycle::deprecated(),
  split_by = NULL,
  feature_merge = FALSE,
  feature_rank = "FEATURE_ID",
  feature_filter = NULL,
  paired = FALSE,
  pvalue.threshold = 0.05,
  logfold.threshold = 0.06,
  abundance.threshold = 0
)

Arguments

condition.group

A character of an existing column name in metaData, wherein the conditions A and B are located.

condition_A

A character (vector) in condition.group.

condition_B

A character (vector) in condition.group.

method

A character to choose the method of fold-change computation (default: "identity").

"identity"

Computes fold-change via log2(condition_A) - log2(condition_B), and will handle zero's to prevent Inf values. Proportional data is also supported and will be automatically detected.

"log"

Computes fold-change via condition_A - condition_B.

How to aggregate the fold-change values for condition_A and condition_B can be controlled with the aggregate_method argument.

aggregate_method

A function to aggregate the fold-change values from multiple samples (default: "median"). options:

"mean"

It takes the arithmetic mean for each feature, separately for condition_A and condition_B.

"median"

It takes the median for each feature, separately for condition_A and condition_B.

"geomean"

It computes the geometric mean of the positive counts, similar to the estimateSizeFactors(), when type = "poscount". The only difference, is that the code is adapted to handle a sparseMatrix.

"none"

No aggreation is applied, the whole matrix is used as it is.

group_by

This argument has been renamed to split_by for more clarity.

split_by

A character variable of an existing column in metaData to split the table in chunks prior to fold-change computation (default: NULL). When disabled then column names will end with _in_all.

feature_merge

A boolean value wether to call $feature_merge() (default: FALSE).

feature_rank

A column in the featureData to use as the feature scope (default: "FEATURE_ID").

feature_filter

A character or vector of characters to remove features via regex substring pattern matching via $feature_merge() (default: NULL).

paired

A boolean value, the paired is only applicable when a SAMPLEPAIR_ID column exists within the metaData (default: FALSE), see $samplepair_subset().

pvalue.threshold

A numeric value used as a p-value threshold to label and color significant features (default: 0.05), see volcano_plot.

logfold.threshold

A numeric value used as a fold-change threshold to label and color significantly expressed features (default: 0.06), see volcano_plot.

abundance.threshold

A numeric value used as an abundance threshold to size the scatter dots based on their mean abundance (default: 0), see volcano_plot.

Returns

A list of components:

split_by subsets

A matrix subset from each split_by separated by condition_A and condition_B.

data

A data.table main output of fold-changes between conditions, contains abundance, fold-change, and homogeneity tests.

volcano_plot

A list of ggplot plots for each contrast of A vs B, number of plots depend on split_by and condition_A input.

Examples

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
features_file <- system.file("extdata", "features.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file,
 featureData = features_file
)
## Method 1: using non-log transformation
obj$scale(method = "tss")

dfe <- obj$foldchange(
 feature_rank = "Genus",
 feature_merge = TRUE,
 method = "identity",
 aggregate_method = "median",
 condition.group = "treatment",
 condition_A = "tumor",
 condition_B = "healthy"
)

## Method 2: using log transformation
obj$reset()
obj$scale(method = "clr")

dfe <- obj$foldchange(
 feature_rank = "Genus",
 feature_merge = TRUE,
 method = "log",
 aggregate_method = "mean",
 condition.group = "treatment",
 condition_A = "tumor",
 condition_B = "healthy"
)

omics$autoFlow()

Automated Omics Analysis only works if there are column names in the metaData with the prefix "CONTRAST_", which is detected via sub-string pattern matching. The transformation of the data is left to the user via the $scale() method. The $autoFlow() incorporates the following functions:

$rankstat()

This function is only applied when feature_ranks is specified, useful in metagenomics, see $rankstat() for more information.

$alpha_diversity()

This function only works with the metagenomics class, uses "shannon" metric, and works for both paired and non-paired data, applied on each "CONTRAST_" column, see $alpha_diversity() for more information.

$ordination()

This function is applied on all classes, multiple distance_metrics can be supplied, and only the Principal Component method ($ordination(method = "pcoa")) is used. Additional arguments can be controlled with distance_metrics, distmat, weighted, perm, threads, see $ordination() for more information. NOTE: perm_design is not supported in $autoFlow().

$composition()

This function is applied on the significant contrasts that are obtained from either $alpha_diversity() or $ordination(). Multiple feature_contrasts can be supplied, by default it only uses the feature_contrasts = "FEATURE_ID". The composition plots are created by default via the composition_plot(group_by) with feature_top = 15. Additional arguments can be controlled with feature_filter, see $composition() for more information.

$foldchange()

This function is applied on the significant contrasts that are obtained from either $alpha_diversity() or $ordination(). Multiple feature_contrasts can be supplied, by default it only uses the feature_contrasts = "FEATURE_ID". Additional arguments can be controlled with fc_method, aggregate_method, pvalue.threshold, logfold.threshold, abundance.threshold, see $foldchange() for more information.

The above functions are called in order, only significant contrasts are further used to create composition and volcano plots. The autoFlow is intended as a first screening of certain contrasts and extra analysis, such as the use of a permutation design are not supported and should be applied by the user.

The report argument controls if an rmarkdown document is created, and with filename the output filename can be specified.

Usage

omics$autoFlow(
  feature_contrast = "FEATURE_ID",
  feature_filter = NULL,
  feature_ranks = NULL,
  distance_metrics = c("bray"),
  distmat = NULL,
  weighted = TRUE,
  fc_method = "log",
  aggregate_method = "median",
  pvalue.threshold = 0.05,
  logfold.threshold = 0.06,
  abundance.threshold = 0,
  perm = 999,
  threads = 1,
  report = TRUE,
  filename = paste0(getwd(), "/report.html")
)

Arguments

feature_contrast

A character vector of feature columns in the featureData to aggregate via $feature_merge() (default: "FEATURE_ID").

feature_filter

A character vector to filter unwanted features, see $feature_merge() (default: NULL).

feature_ranks

A character vector as input to $rankstat() (default: NULL).

distance_metrics

A character vector specifying what (dis)similarity metrics to use in ordination() (default: c("bray")). When you are working with log-transformed data it is advised to use the "euclidean".

distmat

A path to an existing file or a dense/sparse Matrix format to be used in $ordination() (default: NULL).

weighted

A boolean value, whether to compute weighted or unweighted dissimilarities in $ordination() (default: TRUE).

fc_method

A character to choose the method in $foldchange() (default: "identity").

"identity"

Computes fold-change via log2(condition_A) - log2(condition_B), and will handle zero's to prevent Inf values. Proportional data is also supported and will be automatically detected.

"log"

Computes fold-change via condition_A - condition_B.

aggregate_method

A function to aggregate the matrix values in $foldchange() by taking e.g. the median of condition_A and condition_B prior to substraction, or in the case of method = "identity" to take the median of the fold-change log2(median(A)) - log2(median(B)) (default: median).

pvalue.threshold

A numeric value used as a p-value threshold to label and color significant features in $foldchange() (default: 0.05).

logfold.threshold

A numeric value used as a fold-change threshold to label and color significantly expressed features in $foldchange() (default: 0.06).

abundance.threshold

A numeric value used as an abundance threshold to size the scatter dots based on their mean abundance in $foldchange() (default: 0).

perm

A wholenumber, number of permutations to compare against the null hypothesis of adonis2 or anosim in $ordination() (default: 999).

threads

Number of threads to use, only used in $distance() when distmat is not supplied (default: 1).

report

A boolean value to create a HTML markdown report (default: FALSE). If FALSE a nested list of the plots and data is returned.

filename

A character to name the HTML report to be saved in the current working directory (default: paste0(getwd(), "/report.html")). The getwd() is required for rmarkdown to save it in the right path.

Returns

if report = TRUE a HTML report is generated, otherwise a list containing:

plots

  • rankstat_plot as a ggplot.

  • alpha_div_plots as a list of ggplot.

  • pcoa_plots as a nested matrix of lists with ggplot (contrasts x distance_metrics).

  • composition_plots as a nested matrix of lists with ggplot (contrasts x feature_contrasts).

  • Log2FC_plots as a nested matrix of lists with ggplot (contrasts x feature_contrasts).

data

  • alpha_div_data as a list of lists of data and stats.

  • pcoa_data as a nested matrix of lists of stats, dist_mat and pcs (contrasts x distance_metrics).

  • composition_data as a nested matrix of lists of data (contrasts x feature_contrasts).

  • Log2FC_data as a nested matrix of lists of data (contrasts x feature_contrasts).

omics$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

omics$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.

Examples


## ------------------------------------------------
## Method `omics$new()`
## ------------------------------------------------

library("OmicFlow")

## Method 1: load from filepath
metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata_file,
 countData = counts_file
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
#> ✔ countData is loaded.
#> ℹ Created placeholder featureData.

## Method 2: Load from data.frame or matrix
n_cols <- 5
n_rows <- 100
n_vals <- n_cols * n_rows
metadata <- data.frame("SAMPLE_ID" = paste0("Sample_", 1:n_cols))
features <- data.frame("FEATURE_ID" = paste0("protein_", 1:n_rows))
counts <- Matrix::Matrix(
 1:n_vals, nrow = n_rows, ncol = n_cols, 
 dimnames = list(features$FEATURE_ID, metadata$SAMPLE_ID)
)

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 featureData = features, # optional
 countData = counts
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
#> ✔ featureData is loaded.
#> ✔ countData is loaded.

## Method 3: you have features and counts in a single data.frame
metadata <- data.frame(SAMPLE_ID = c("S1", "S2", "S3"))
counts <- data.frame(
 S1 = c(2,3,0), 
 S2 = c(2,"",1), 
 S3 = c(2,1,NA), 
 proteins = c("ZEB1", "ZEB2", "MAPK")
)

obj <- omics$new(
 metaData = metadata,
 countData = counts
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
#> ℹ Placeholder featureData extracted from countData.
#> ✔ countData is loaded.

## Method `omics$copy()`

library("OmicFlow")

metadata_file <- system.file("extdata", "metadata.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")
counts_file <- system.file("extdata", "counts.tsv", package = "OmicFlow")

 countData = counts_file
)
#> ✔ metaData template passed the JSON validation.
#> ℹ Checking for duplicated identifiers ..
#> ✔ countData is loaded.
#> ℹ Created placeholder featureData.

# Perform a modification and copy
obj$scale()

cloned <- obj$copy(deep=TRUE)
cloned$scale(method = "clr")
cloned$reset() # resets to data after clone creation.

 aggregate_method = "mean",
 condition.group = "treatment",
 condition_A = "tumor",
 condition_B = "healthy"
)
